reason: The original idea is repaired by fixing one positive tolerance, as required by the negation of uniform convergence, and first identifying the unique pointwise limit.
text:
For each \(x\in[0,1)\), we have \(x^n\to0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
Fix \(\varepsilon_0=\tfrac12\). For every \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), take \(n=N\) and \(x_N=2^{-1/N}\in[0,1)\). Then \(f(x_N)=0\) and
\[
|f_N(x_N)-f(x_N)|=x_N^N=\tfrac12.
\]
Hence, for every \(N\), there exist \(n\ge N\) and \(x\in[0,1]\) for which \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon_0\). Therefore \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\).
